idiom_name: hand-written forwarding wrapper implementing the target interface (or a template mixin)
implementation_notes: C++ has no reflection and no standard annotation processing, so the interceptor is a hand-written forwarding class: it implements the same interface as the target, records the event and delegates to the wrapped instance, with std::function (or a template parameter) injecting the audit sink so the wrapper stays independent of the logging backend. Where the audited type is a template or the hierarchy can be changed, a template mixin that derives from the implementation and overrides only the audited methods replaces the runtime interface with compile-time forwarding. The classic forwarding wrapper remains the right choice when auditing must be applied to an existing hierarchy without rebuilding it - and it is the only portable option.
pitfalls: Store a reference or pointer to the target, never a copy - copying slices the implementation, and a dangling reference after the target dies is the classic failure mode of hand-written wrappers.
Hand-forwarding a wide interface is error-prone: a method that is not overridden silently forwards unaudited, and the compiler will not warn about it.

An exception raised by the audit sink must not change the outcome of the audited operation unintentionally: decide whether an audit failure is fail-open or fail-closed and mark the wrapper's exception specification accordingly.
